# Decisions: session-naming

- 2026-09-28T08:46:13.764Z — rule: **A session's name reaches the host only as hookSpecificOutput.sessionTitle from a hook sofar already runs, never by writing the host's registry, and never over a title the operator typed (/rename, --name).** — chose **SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit return {"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName", "additionalContext"?, "sessionTitle"}} for Claude Code, with sessionTitle = "<slug> <focus task id>" (the slug alone when the record has no open task), and only when the payload's session_title is absent, the host's derived "<cwd folder>-<2 hex>" name, or a title whose first token is an initiative of this repo. Otherwise the output stays the byte-identical plain stdout of today. Cursor and Codex outputs never carry it.** over (a) a second SessionStart hook entry just for the title — one more process per event on the 100ms path and a settings.json change every init/doctor must mirror; (b) writing ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json ourselves — peer-messaging D1 forbids touching the registry; (c) emitting the title unconditionally — it would overwrite a /rename or --name the operator chose on the next prompt. because Read from the claude 2.1.283 binary: both hooks receive session_title on stdin and both accept hookSpecificOutput.sessionTitle, which the host applies as the session's name and title (nameSource "hook") — the same address SendMessage, ListAgents and the sidebar use. The host is idempotent on an unchanged title, and Claude Code has no additionalContext spill (that threshold is Codex's), so the JSON form costs nothing over plain stdout. The slug and focus task are already in memory when the digest renders, so no new read, fold or spawn lands on the hook path; the only new I/O is one stat of .sofar/initiatives/<first token> to recognise a title as ours. Host derivation stays the host's: sofar hands over a string and writes nothing.
